reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 20 question-paper pages and PDF pages 1–23 of the combined Higher Level scheme (cover, notes, contents, the Paper 1 title page 5, the scale table on page 6, the summary of mark allocations on page 7, every Paper 1 model solution and marking note on pages 8–21, the blank page 22 and the Paper 2 title page 23). Each task boundary is the published scale beside its model solution, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: The paper is 300 marks: candidates answer all nine questions (Section A Q1–6, 25 marks each; Section B Q7 55 marks, Q8 40 marks, Q9 55 marks). Every question is retained.
33 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 7.

Paper 1 bands from the 2018 scale table on scheme page 6: 5B 0,2,5; 5C 0,3,4,5; 10C 0,4,8,10; 10D 0,3,5,8,10; 15C 0,5,10,15; 15D 0,5,7,11,15; 20D 0,5,10,15,20. Every part prints the same ladder beside its scale.

This paper had no authored cards before this review; all 33 units are new. Marking points are lifted line by line from the scheme (read through the glyph repair map) and labelled with the part of the scheme they come from. Lines whose stacked-fraction numerator extracts as a lone "1" (the f(x), f′(x) and f′′(x) working in Q8, one line each in Q7(e)(ii) and Q9(c)(i)) cannot be checked as text, and the model solutions of Q9(a) (a table) and Q6(b)(ii), Q7(c) and Q7(d) (graphs) are printed as images. Those parts, and Q3(b) whose integral limits the text layer cannot carry, eleven in all (Q3(b), Q6(b)(ii), Q7(c), Q7(d), Q7(e)(ii), Q8(a)–(d), Q9(a), Q9(c)(i)), carry the SEC’s own print of their scheme row (model solution and every credit band), cropped from the scheme PDF and shown only after the reveal. The Q6(b)(i) integral limits are named in the row label.

The question booklet is LC003ALP100EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003ALP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 2. Scheme page references are PDF positions (printed page number + 3); question-paper PDF positions match the printed page numbers.

cards.questionText: Solve the simultaneous equations. 2x + 3y − z = −4; 3x + 2y + 2z = 14; x − 3z = −13.
Solve the inequality (2x − 3)/(x + 2) ≥ 3, where x ∈ ℝ and x ≠ −2.
The first three terms of a geometric series are x², 5x − 8, and x + 8, where x ∈ ℝ. Use the common ratio to show that x³ − 17x² + 80x − 64 = 0.
If f(x) = x³ − 17x² + 80x − 64, x ∈ ℝ, show that f(1) = 0, and find another value of x for which f(x) = 0.

cards.stem: The first three terms of a geometric series are x², 5x − 8, and x + 8, where x ∈ ℝ. Part (b): If f(x) = x³ − 17x² + 80x − 64, x ∈ ℝ, show that f(1) = 0, and find another value of x for which f(x) = 0.
cards.questionText: In the case of one of the values of x from part (b), the terms in part (a) will generate a geometric series with a finite sum to infinity. Find this value of x and hence find the sum to infinity.
Let h(x) = cos(2x), where x ∈ ℝ. A tangent is drawn to the graph of h(x) at the point where x = π/3. Find the angle that this tangent makes with the positive sense of the x-axis.
